93413.synopsis:
Five years since being summoned to another world, Seo-ah had somehow managed to save it.
They were incredibly grateful, and now they wanted to send her back. She would even receive ample rewards.
But… does she really have to go back? There’s no one waiting for her there, and here, she had someone she loves.
“The summoning circle that brought you here is the same as the one for the reverse summoning. Both the caster and the summoned must be pure.”
The solution was simple: she just needed to lose her purity.
And as luck would have it, the caster of the reverse summoning was none other than the man she liked.
If she was going to give up her purity, what better way than to enjoy it with him?
The problem was that this man happened to be the High Priest, an icon of purity and virtue.
“Your Holiness, I… I feel… hot. Something’s strange… down there…”
“This is purely to heal you. There’s no other meaning here.”
She tried every trick to bring him down…
“Seo-ah, it would be best for you to rest deeply. When you wake up, everything will be fine.”
“Please feel free to use the bed on your own. I’ll be spending the night in prayer.”
Breaking through the wall of kindness and his iron will was proving anything but easy.
With the reverse summoning ritual drawing nearer every moment, can Seo-ah successfully win him over and find a way to stay in this world?
*
“I was determined to send you back. To your homeland, which you longed for so much—a place where you wouldn’t have to bear any burden. However…”
Somehow, his hands had wrapped tightly around Seo-ah’s shoulders and waist.
Holding her closely in his arms, he looked down at her bewildered expression, his blue eyes clouded with emotion.
Below, faint moisture glistened along his eyelids, a shimmer in the moonlight that gradually thickened.
“Seo-ah… Please, do not forgive me for this.”
He lowered his head and once again captured her lips.
As he closed his eyes, a tear escaped from beneath his silver lashes, tracing a line down his cheek.

117221.synopsis:
An Qing traveled through time in an instant, transforming from a doctoral student at an agricultural college into a Mongolian princess during the Kangxi era of the Qing Dynasty, suddenly arranged to marry the Fifth Prince.
Looking at the towering walls of the Forbidden City, An Qing couldn’t help but hold her forehead and sigh. Everyone in this palace had minds as intricate as sieves, and in front of them, she was nothing but a naive innocent.
Fortunately, An Qing’s luck wasn’t too bad – she was assigned to the Fifth Prince Yinqi, who wasn’t involved in the succession struggle. Her maternal family was also the most capable branch of the Khorchin tribe, highly valued by Emperor Kangxi.
Anyway, palace intrigue was impossible for her to engage in. Wouldn’t it be wonderful to simply close the door and live her own wealthy and comfortable life?
So,
While the side concubines and geges (Low-ranking Concubines) used every means to compete for favor, An Qing ate, drank, and farmed.
While her sisters-in-law busied themselves showing off their virtue and filial piety, An Qing ate, drank, and farmed.
While the various princes were busy forming factions and fighting for power, An Qing pulled Yinqi along to eat, drink, and farm together.
But who would have known that An Qing, whom no one in the palace took seriously, would not only casually save the premium peonies used for sacrificial ceremonies that symbolized good fortune, but also solve the agricultural pest and disease problems like “rice blast” and “ghost wheat” that had troubled emperors and court officials throughout history.
Not to mention the succession of high-yield crops that appeared in her estate…
Many years later, tales spread throughout the countryside of a renowned “Goddess of Agriculture.” Tens of thousands of common people voluntarily erected monuments in her honor.
It was said that this “Goddess of Agriculture” was a precious lady from the Forbidden City, yet she preferred to spend her time in fields and farmlands, simply because she said… she wanted all the children in the world to have enough to eat.
—
Yinqi had grown up under the Empress Dowager’s care since childhood, deeply influenced by the old lady. From a young age, he had a generous, benevolent nature and disliked conflict.
But the imperial family could never escape power struggles. Faced with father-son discord, fraternal conflicts, and factional disputes, Yinqi found himself in a difficult position, walking on thin ice, his heart tormented day and night.
Until An Qing came to his side. Gradually, her calm and easygoing nature, every smile and frown, became his salvation.
From then on, he devoted all his efforts to withdrawing safely from the sword-like conflicts of this power struggle, just so he could give her a peaceful and smooth life.
Three meals and four seasons, spring planting and autumn harvest – looking at the layers of wheat waves in the fields, then turning back to see his wife and children beside him, Yinqi found an unprecedented peace in his heart.

[Because you excel at and enjoy collecting garbage, your hobby has been acknowledged by the Sea God. Congratulations, you have awakened the talent: Scavenger.] 
[Scavenger: +5 initial backpack slots. When obtaining any equipment, +35% critical chance.] 
***
‘One more brick today, one more plank tomorrow.’
With her scavenger talent, He Ni painstakingly pieced together a shabby little shack on the sea.
Meanwhile, a top player flaunted a luxury yacht.
“This ship still feels a bit small,” he said.
He Ni looked at her floating pile of junk and sighed.
The same player roasted a whole lamb to perfection.
“Tastes just average,” he muttered.
He Ni, holding her dry strips of smoked meat, could only stare and swallow hungrily.
***
Later, when the rankings were revealed, He Ni nearly fainted in shock.
How could someone like her—living such a miserable life—be sitting at the top of the Wealth, Power, and Survival Leaderboards?
And that so-called “top player” who seemed untouchable… secretly sent her a private message:
